survey.readings: Axis 56 degrees counter-clockwise from east, front to the south-west. Hall 23 m wide; front tower blocks 5 m square at the corners with a 3 m recess between; back corner blocks lower with a stuccoed centre. 3DBAG: hall eaves 21.2 m, hipped ridge 27.8 m, tower stages to 36.5-37.4 m (caps), back corner blocks about 15 m, back centre to about 21 m.

facadeRhythm.south-west front (Waterlooplein): Symmetric, cream stucco. Two tower blocks, each with Ionic corner pilasters and a blind round-arched niche over a sunk panel, cornice at 16 m. Between them a portico of four grey stone Ionic columns, one bay deep, grey entablature with the inscription frieze, stucco pediment with a cartouche, slate-roofed. Behind the columns a grey wall: central door, a niche with a statue over it. Above: attic with a balustrade and the statue of Christ. Towers: a square open stage (arched opening per face, slate-blue panels flanking, balustraded sill) with a pediment on each face, a narrower open stage of the same pattern, a slate ogee cap, ball and cross.
facadeRhythm.flanks (north-west and south-east): Brown brick, three tall round-arched windows with small-paned glazing and light bars, cream cornice at 21.2 m, stone plinth; the stucco tower block shows at the front end, the lower brick corner block at the back.
facadeRhythm.north-east back (Jodenbreestraat): Symmetric. Stuccoed frontispiece with four pilasters, a round-arched niche with a statue, entablature and pediment with an oculus; either side a lower brick corner block with a cream cornice and a hipped slate roof, each with a door at the foot and two windows above on its outer faces.
facadeRhythm.roofs: Hall: one hipped slate roof (eaves 21.2 m, ridge 27.8 m). Back corner blocks: low hipped slate roofs. Frontispiece: pitched roof behind the pediment. Nothing from the 3DBAG roof meshes.

decisions: Plan and heights from BAG/3DBAG; all roofs and facades from intent and photographs.
Bell-tower openings are dark panels, not real holes.
Statues are simple lathed figures; the inscription and pediment carving are not modelled.
The north-west flank is taken as the mirror of the south-east (RCE 20013478 shows the same three windows).
